title: Low Altitude Air Defense (LAAD) Enhancement Training Instructor (LETI) (GySgt to Sgt) NMOS (7212), DC AVN
raw_text:
11. MOS 7276, Low Altitude Air Defense (LAAD) Enhancement Training
Instructor (LETI) (GySgt to Sgt) NMOS (7212), DC AVN

    a. Summary. LETIs train LAAD Marines on LAAD equipment, tactics,
techniques and procedures, and serve as LAAD employment subject matter
experts to advise supported units.




                                           3-452                        Enclosure (1)
 3147                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess PMOS 7212.

            (2) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 LETI Course (code LETI).

            (2) Upon approval by APX7.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Assist Weapons and Tactics Instructors (WTI) in executing the
LAAD unit’s Weapons and Tactics Training Program (WTTP).

            (2) Perform instruction of LAAD core and mission skills.

            (3) Serve as LAAD employment subject matter expert.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.
common_text: The Air Control, Air Traffic Control, Air Support, And Antiair Warfare OccFld includes the operation and management of the air command and control functions associated with the Marine Aircraft Wing. Qualifications required include manual dexterity for man-machine interface, highly developed visual/auditory skills, the ability to communicate effectively with radios, and the leadership and skills to work effectively as a member of a command and control team. The duties involve skills and procedures that are initially acquired through formal schools and further developed by individual and team training. Air Control, air traffic control, air support and antiair warfare Marines will be required to learn the emplacement, cabling orientation and operation of air command, control, traffic control, and antiair warfare defense systems and equipment. Entry- Level assignments include LAAD Gunner, Air Command and Control Operator, Air Traffic Controller, and Air Support Operations Operator. A wide variety of FMF billets are available in the OccFld in the active and reserve forces at group, squadron/battalion, or battery level. Numerous non-FMF assignments also exist at the Marine Corps Systems Command and Marine Corps Air Stations worldwide as instructors at MOS-producing schools. Marines will participate in routine air command and control functions while training for a designated MOS within the OccFld (see figure 3-38 for additional information concerning the career/grade structure and schooling of these Marines).

The Air Control, Air Traffic Control, Air Support, And Antiair Warfare OccFld includes the operation and management of the air command and control functions associated with the Marine Aircraft Wing. Qualifications required include manual dexterity for man-machine interface, highly developed visual/auditory skills, the ability to communicate effectively with radios, and the leadership and skills to work effectively as a member of a command and control team. The duties involve skills and procedures that are initially acquired through formal schools and further developed by individual and team training. Air Control, air traffic control, air support and antiair warfare Marines will be required to learn the emplacement, cabling orientation and operation of air command, control, traffic control, and antiair warfare defense systems and equipment. Entry- Level assignments include LAAD Gunner, Air Command and Control Operator, Air Traffic Controller, and Air Support Operations Operator. A wide variety of FMF billets are available in the OccFld in the active and reserve forces at group, squadron/battalion, or battery level. Numerous non-FMF assignments also exist at the Marine Corps Systems Command and Marine Corps Air Stations worldwide as instructors at MOS-producing schools. Marines will participate in routine air command and control functions while training for a designated MOS within the OccFld (see figure 3-38 for additional information concerning the career/grade structure and schooling of these Marines).

11. MOS 7276, Low Altitude Air Defense (LAAD) Enhancement Training Instructor (LETI) (GySgt to Sgt) NMOS (7212), DC AVN a. Summary. LETIs train LAAD Marines on LAAD equipment, tactics, techniques and procedures, and serve as LAAD employment subject matter experts to advise supported units. b. Prerequisites (1) Must possess PMOS 7212. (2) Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility. c. Requirements (1) Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 LETI Course (code LETI). (2) Upon approval by APX7. d. Duties (1) Assist Weapons and Tactics Instructors (WTI) in executing the LAAD unit’s Weapons and Tactics Training Program (WTTP). (2) Perform instruction of LAAD core and mission skills. (3) Serve as LAAD employment subject matter expert.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
